newsitem.title: RWANDA: Tutsis battle Zairean troops in border town.
newsitem.headline: Tutsis battle Zairean troops in border town.

text.p: Banyamulenge ethnic Tutsis battled Zairean troops around the eastern Zairean border town of Uvira on Saturday, displacing thousands of refugees, a spokesman for the U.N. refugee agency said.

Paul Stromberg, spokesman for the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) in neighbouring Rwanda, told Reuters the fighting first erupted near Zaire's Luvengi refugee camp, home to Rwandans and Burundians displaced by ethnic conflict in their motherlands.
"Renewed fighting has broken out this morning between the Banyamulenge and Zairean armed forces near Luvengi refugee camp," Stromberg said.
Stromberg gave no details, saying the refugee agency had failed to reach the fighting area.
Another aid worker in the Rwandan capital Kigali told Reuters the situation in the eastern Zaire area was very confused and that fighting was heavy.
Humanitarian sources in Bukavu, eastern Zaire, said on Saturday that at least 28 civilians had been killed around the village of Kiliba in fighting between Zairean soldiers and ethnic Tutsi rebels.
Stromberg said Zairean residents had taken to the streets to demonstrate against the Banyamulenge -- an ethnic Tutsi group which left Rwanda for Zaire at the end of the 18th century.
The Banyamulenge are fighting for their right to Zairean citizenship. They say they are discriminated against by indigenous Zaireans on the basis of language and ethnicity.
On Friday, up to 26,400 mainly Burundi refugees fled their camp near Uvira after fighting between the Zairean military and Banyamulenge left three dead, senior aid workers said.
The fighting was the second major round in Zaire in a week. Last Sunday about 20,000 Hutu refugees from Burundi fled their camp in eastern Zaire after it was attacked by armed men.

Fighting between Banyamulenge rebels and Zairean authorities trying to drive an estimated 200,000 Banyamulenge from a plateau west of Lake Tanganyika has left Zaire's South Kivu region in a virtual state of war.
Some 220,000 Rwandan and Burundian refugees languish in camps north of Uvira, a town in the delta to the northwest of Lake Tanganyika surrounded by steep hills.
Zaire accuses the Tutsi-dominated army of Rwanda of training and arming the Banyamulenge guerrillas.

Analysts fear that the Banyamulenge crisis, ethnic conflict in Rwanda and Burundi, could degenerate into a regional war. Eastern Zaire is home to over a million Rwandan and Burundian Hutu refugees who fled Tutsi military authorities in their respective countries.

Both Rwanda and Burundi accuse Zaire of supporting Hutu rebels waging war in their homelands. The Hutus from Rwanda fled in 1994 after Tutsi rebels seized power and overthrew the Hutu administration of Juvenal Habyarimana.
Millions of Hutus -- including Habyarimana's 40,000-strong -- army then fled to neighbouring Zaire and Tanzania. Aid workers say the Hutus are reshaping themselves for a military return to Rwanda.

Eastern Zaire is also home to training bases for Burundian Hutu rebels fighting the tiny country's Tutsi military junta. The rebels, mainly those belonging to Leonard Nyangoma's National Council for the Defence of Democracy (CNDD), are fighting for a greater political stake in their country.
The Banyamulenge problem has in recent weeks resulted in heavy gunfire exchanges between Zaire's ragged army and Rwanda's battle-hardened army.
